news.headline: A Giant Sunshade Gets Ready for an Asteroid Hunter
news.body: NASA is building a space telescope called NEO Surveyor to find asteroids and comets that are hard to spot from Earth. Its biggest part is a sunshade that stands 20 feet tall, taller than a giraffe! The sunshade blocks the Sun's glare to keep the telescope cool, and it is covered with 864 solar cells that make all of the spacecraft's power. Workers just finished adding those solar cells, bringing the telescope one step closer to launch.

news.headline: Kid Hula Hoopers Spin Their Way to Six World Records
news.body: Young hula hoopers from a club called the Chennai Hoopers traveled from India, the United Kingdom, and the United States to London to try for world records. They set six of them! One girl spun a hoop around her neck for more than 15 minutes while sitting in the splits. Another kept a hoop spinning while standing on one leg, about two and a half spins every second.

news.headline: Two New Jelly-Like Creatures Found Deep in the Sea
news.body: Scientists at the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute discovered two kinds of deep-sea animals nobody knew about before. They are siphonophores, see-through ocean drifters that are related to jellyfish. One has stretchy orange stomachs, and the other has a fiery red body. The team found them by studying underwater robot videos and museum samples, plus clues hidden in the animals' DNA.

fun_fact: Asteroids can have their own moons! Scientists have found hundreds of asteroids with tiny moons circling around them. 🌑

joke.q: Why did the hula hoop go to the doctor?
joke.a: It was feeling a little run-down from going in circles all day! ⭕
